articles.title: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for AI Agent Management Platforms
articles.context: It brings supported agents from Microsoft, customer-built agents, local agents found on devices, and partner clouds and frameworks into one registry
articles.full_text:
Microsoft has been named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for AI Agent Management Platforms. We believe this recognition reflects Microsoft’s approach to helping organizations manage, secure, and scale their AI investments through Microsoft Agent 365.

Figure 1: Gartner, Magic Quadrant for AI Agent Management Platforms, October 27, 2026.

Monitor and manage agents with Microsoft Agent 365

When we introduced Agent 365, we started with a simple concept: agents should be managed with the same rigor you already apply to users, apps, and devices, using the infrastructure and protections that already run your business. Since then, more than 50 million agents have been registered in Agent 365.1

Here’s what we believe made the difference.

We started with identity, not monitoring

Many approaches to managing agents focus on monitoring after an agent is running. Microsoft’s approach begins with identity. With Microsoft Entra Agent ID, every agent in the organization is assigned a unique agent ID, associated with an owner and purpose, and the right access controls based on its needs.

This enables organizations to apply established identity and access policies to both people and agents. Agent access policies are dynamically adjusted as risk signals and conditions change. Organizations can manage agent access through the Microsoft identity infrastructure they already use for their workforce.

We built on what you already trust

Rather than building a separate platform, Agent 365 extends the tools IT and security teams already use every day: Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Intune, and the Microsoft 365 admin center.

That decision shapes the experience. Microsoft data protection, compliance, and security capabilities can help organizations extend familiar controls to supported agent scenarios.2

We meet agents where they are

Agents won’t come from one platform, so Agent 365 is designed to support a broad ecosystem. It brings supported agents from Microsoft, customer-built agents, local agents found on devices, and partner clouds and frameworks into one registry. Current integrations include Agentforce, Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Databricks, Google Gemini, and Google Vertex, with more planned integrations coming soon, including OpenAI, ServiceNow, and Snowflake. Agent 365 also integrates agents built using supported open-source frameworks with the Agent 365 software development kit (SDK).

For additional agent patterns, including local and previously unknown agents discovered through Microsoft Security sensors, Agent 365 supports fit-for-purpose identity types so they can be represented in the registry with appropriate ownership, activity, and risk context. Microsoft is also previewing discovery of cloud agents, extending visibility beyond known and integrated agents. Together, native integrations, connectors, and security sensors help organizations discover and govern more of their agent estate across cloud and device environments.

There’s more to do

Agent 365 moved quickly from introduction to general availability, and we haven’t slowed down. We’re proud of this recognition, and we know there’s more work ahead. We are expanding discovery to 35 additional local agent types, bringing the total to 60, along with adding support to discover unknown agents, bringing these agents under management, as well as extending policy coverage and controls for both managed and unmanaged agents, including third-party agents.

But, visibility and controls are only the beginning. Customers have asked for more automated support for agent governance and security. The new Agent 365 Action Center helps IT and security leaders move from reactive alerts to prescriptive actions, like cleaning up inactive agents, reassigning ownerless agents, or automatically blocking agents based on risk.

We’re also advancing cost management, task classification, and value calculation to help organizations understand how agents are being used, what they cost, and the value they deliver.

Our promise hasn’t changed: to help every organization move from experimenting with agents to running them confidently, with the same rigor, protections, and accountability that already run the enterprise. We believe Agent 365 enables any organization to deploy AI at scale.

Get started

Get your copy of the Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Agent Management Platforms.

Learn more about Microsoft Agent 365.

Get Agent 365 with Microsoft 365 E7, or as an add-on to Microsoft 365 E5.

Attending Microsoft Ignite 2026? Join us to learn more about what’s next for Agent 365.

Get started with Microsoft Agent 365

To learn more about Microsoft Security solutions, visit our website. Bookmark the Security blog to keep up with our expert coverage on security matters. Also, follow us on LinkedIn (Microsoft Security) and X (@MSFTSecurity) for the latest news and updates on cybersecurity.

Gartner, Magic Quadrant for AI Management Platforms, Andrei Razvan Sachelarescu, Lucas Kobat, Gilbert van der Heiden, Max Goss, October 27, 2026.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Fiddler to Deliver Falcon Observe for AI Agent Observability
articles.context: It will become part of the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform as CrowdStrike Falcon® Observe, generally available in Q4 FY27
articles.full_text:
I am delighted to announce CrowdStrike’s intent to acquire Fiddler at Fal.Con EU 2026. Fiddler, a leader in AI observability, will help ensure enterprise AI agents act as intended with pre-deployment evaluation and continuous behavioral monitoring as part of the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform.

Every business deploying AI agents asks the same questions: What are our agents doing? Are they staying on task? Are they acting in a way that could put the business at risk?

AI agents don’t have to be compromised to be dangerous. Those that stay within their guardrails can make a bad decision or take harmful action using valid credentials and approved enterprise tools. Businesses must be able to trace agents’ activity and explain anomalies as these concerns become top of mind among auditors, regulators, board members, and risk managers.

Enterprise AI safety requires a comprehensive approach: Evaluate agents before deployment, understand their decisions and actions, and continuously monitor their behavior. AI observability provides a lens into agent behavior before and after they ship. AI explainability shows why agents made their decisions and where their actions may have gone awry.

Fiddler delivers both. It will become part of the CrowdStrike Falcon® platform as CrowdStrike Falcon® Observe, generally available in Q4 FY27. With this acquisition, CrowdStrike will extend our AI security capabilities beyond protecting AI systems into proving businesses can safely use AI agents every day.

Building AI Trust in the Agentic Enterprise

Unlike traditional software, AI agents can make autonomous decisions, invoke tools, and take actions across enterprise systems. If software can act autonomously, security needs a record of those actions: what each agent decided, how it acted, what it changed, and the tools it used. They must know whether the agent made the correct decisions to follow its intended task.

As an example: Consider an AI agent using approved tools and valid credentials to process a customer refund. The agent makes an incorrect decision and approves a refund that violates company policy. Traditional security controls may see legitimate activity, but AI explainability reveals why the agent made that decision and where its behavior went wrong.

Fiddler provides AI observability for the agentic era. It helps organizations identify misaligned agents before they are deployed and continues to monitor agent behavior post-deployment so businesses have full visibility into what they’re doing and why.

Before deployment, teams can compare prompts, models, and configurations to evaluate whether agents perform intended tasks safely and accurately before they reach production.

After deployment, teams can trace agents’ decisions and reasoning paths across the full agent hierarchy to detect issues like behavioral drift and unintended actions before they cause harm. Fiddler reconstructs the agent’s decision-making process so teams can trace each failure to the step that caused it.

Fiddler supports auditable AI governance across organizations’ existing agents and tools. Its granular view of agents’ decision-making covers first-party and third-party agents across the enterprise so teams have the data they need to support compliance and audits. Businesses also gain explainability across the frameworks they run, as Fiddler enables teams to instrument agents through OpenTelemetry and supports LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Strands, and Google ADK.

As part of the Falcon platform, Fiddler will connect AI agent intent and behavior with Falcon security telemetry across endpoints, identity, cloud, and runtime environments. This will help security teams understand why an agent took an action and what happened across the enterprise as a result. By connecting agent decisions with enterprise security context, CrowdStrike will provide visibility that goes beyond standalone AI observability.

CrowdStrike Delivers the Enterprise AI Control Plane

This milestone extends CrowdStrike’s leadership in protecting the agentic enterprise. Our acquisition of Fiddler, together with CrowdStrike Falcon® Guardian innovations announced today, will bring comprehensive AI security and safety solutions to the Falcon platform.

CrowdStrike can already establish AI agents as trusted identities, connect those identities to the humans operating them, grant access to business systems based on real-time risk, and secure AI agents at runtime. Fiddler will extend the Falcon platform to the earliest stages of the agent lifecycle, before deployment, to monitor their behavior before and after production, and explain the decisions they make.

Falcon Guardian protects AI agents from attacks and misuse. Falcon Observe evaluates and explains whether agents behave as intended. Together, they secure AI operations in the agentic enterprise.

Forward-Looking Statements

This blog contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding the closing and benefits of the proposed acquisition. These statements involve risks and uncertainties, and actual results may differ materially. There are a number of risks that could cause actual results to differ materially, including the satisfaction of the acquisition’s closing conditions, our ability to integrate Fiddler, and other risks described in the filings we make with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission from time to time.

articles.title: Cybersecurity M&A Roundup: 37 Deals Announced in October 2026
articles.context: Here are some of the most important cybersecurity M&A deals announced in October 2026: Absolute Security acquires FirmGuard Endpoint security and cyber resilience firm Absolute...
articles.full_text:
SecurityWeek tracked 37 cybersecurity merger and acquisition (M&A) deals announced in October 2026.

For a look at last year’s activity, see SecurityWeek’s 2025 Cybersecurity M&A Report, which covers more than 420 deals.

Here are some of the most important cybersecurity M&A deals announced in October 2026:

Absolute Security acquires FirmGuard

Endpoint security and cyber resilience firm Absolute Security has acquired FirmGuard, the UEFI BIOS firmware security and management business of Phoenix Technologies. Absolute will integrate FirmGuard with its firmware-embedded Absolute Persistence technology, adding below-the-OS management, continuous firmware integrity monitoring and patching, and compliance enforcement.

Aikido Security acquires OutKept and Cyberly

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Belgian application security unicorn Aikido Security has acquired OutKept and Cyberly and used the two startups to launch Noon, a workforce security business. OutKept is based in Belgium and provides phishing simulations and security awareness training. Poland’s Cyberly develops AI-powered attack simulations and tools for tracking employee AI usage. Both deals closed in September but weren’t made public until October.

Anthropic to acquire Opaque Systems

AI company Anthropic has agreed to acquire Opaque Systems, a confidential AI company that grew out of research at UC Berkeley. Anthropic has described the deal as licensing Opaque’s technology and hiring some of its engineers, reportedly including CEO Aaron Fulkerson and CTO Rishabh Poddar. Financial terms weren’t disclosed.

Cohere to acquire AISLE

Canadian AI developer Cohere has signed a letter of intent to acquire AISLE, a startup whose autonomous AI systems find and help patch vulnerabilities in critical software. AISLE’s roughly 50 employees will join Cohere, which is setting up a cybersecurity unit called Cohere Cyber. AISLE CEO Ondřej Vlček, the former CEO of Avast, will become its senior vice president.

Hex-Rays to acquire HexAI

Hex-Rays, the Belgian company behind the IDA Pro reverse engineering tool, has agreed to acquire HexAI, an Israeli startup founded in 2025. HexAI’s AI agents analyze source code and binaries to uncover vulnerabilities, malware and backdoors. The deal is reportedly worth $30 million to $35 million. Hex-Rays plans to grow HexAI’s Israeli operations and build new AI-powered research tools.

IonQ has to acquire Elisity

Quantum computing company IonQ has agreed to acquire zero trust security firm Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-based earnouts. IonQ will combine its post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution technology with Elisity’s IdentityGraph platform, which enforces least-privilege access for users, devices, workloads and AI agents. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Proofpoint to acquire Varonis

Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint has agreed to acquire data security company Varonis for roughly $6.3 billion in cash. Together, the companies want to offer a single platform for discovering and protecting sensitive data, controlling access to it, and preventing data loss as organizations adopt AI.

Innovator recognizes organizations introducing new ideas, technologies, or approaches that meaningfully advance cybersecurity

Winners: Sun Chemical; Taiwan Mobile; MITSUI SUMITOMO INSURANCE Agency Service; Qassim University

Visionary honors organizations that are transforming a bold cybersecurity vision into measurable progress

Winners: Pegasystems; SoftBank

Cyber Defender celebrates those demonstrating an exceptional commitment to protecting people, operations, and digital environments

Rachel Jin, CEO of TrendAI™: "This year's Cybersecurity Excellence Awards represent the next generation of security-first leaders who understand that cyber resilience is not a compliance checkbox, but a competitive advantage. These customers have transformed how they approach risk, turning threat intelligence into innovation, and weaving security into the fabric of business strategy. That's what true excellence looks like."

In an increasingly hostile and difficult threat environment, we are able to support the delicate act of healing without undue burden, thanks to organizational backing at all levels and TrendAI's feature rich product suite."

articles.title: JFrog Names Nine Global Winners for Inaugural Software Supply Chain Excellence Awards
articles.context: This year’s JFrog Software Supply Chain Excellence Award winners are working to reduce their exposure to these emerging threats by building a system of record that governs and...
articles.full_text:
JFrog announced completion of the first-ever Software Supply Chain Excellence Awards, recognizing the teams who have turned their software supply chain into a competitive advantage – unifying development, security and operations around a governed, automated ecosystem that delivers trusted software at scale.

The nine honorees span the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, across three categories: Unified Platform, Trusted AI Adoption, and Software Supply Chain Security.

“Agents now write, review and deploy code faster than ever, while malicious AI models, agent skills and extensions are turning up in the registries developers use daily. Increasing regulations require proof at every step – from code to runtime,” said Roie Shorer, Chief Growth Officer at JFrog. “The companies that pull ahead in the AI era will be those going beyond simply automating for speed and scale. They will be the ones who can see exactly what’s shipping and why, as they bring trust, control and adaptability to their development operations. This year’s winners didn’t just add tools; they established a single source of truth where developers, security, and compliance teams can operate using the same data and the same rules. We’re very proud of all of them and thrilled to be part of their journey.”

Software supply chains are being put under new strain as developer teams grapple with AI-era software challenges. In its 2026 Software Supply Chain Security report, JFrog identified over 900 malicious AI agent skills carrying high-impact payloads alongside 495 malicious AI models on Hugging Face and 56 malicious extensions on OpenVSX. Attackers are no longer just targeting code; they are targeting the autonomous tools that write, review, and deploy it.

This year’s JFrog Software Supply Chain Excellence Award winners are working to reduce their exposure to these emerging threats by building a system of record that governs and secures artifacts from end-to-end – mastering the AI surge with speed and trust.

THE CONVERGENCE AWARD

The Convergence Award recognizes teams that unify a fragmented software delivery workflow – bringing previously disconnected repositories, scanners and tools into a single governed system of record.

Here are the winners:

Ford (Americas): Ford Motor Company has more than 15,000 developers spread across 80-plus global plants, which previously ran on separate repository tools and scanners with no shared visibility between them. By consolidating operations into a unified ecosystem with the JFrog Platform, Ford reduced tool sprawl and turned multiple blind spots into a single pane of glass view for IT and security teams. As a result, the team now manages more than 43 million artifacts on the JFrog Platform with 99.99% uptime. The team credits the consolidation with recapturing an estimated $8 million a year in developer productivity.

SCHOTTEL Industries (EMEA): Schottel replaced fragmented artifact storage and open-source consumption with the JFrog Platform. Over six months it delivered more than 32,000 artifacts, curated over 2,300 open-source packages and automatically blocked more than 900 risky ones. Manual dependency approval processes that previously delayed developers by months were replaced by automated governance and security controls, enabling faster adoption of new technologies while helping maintain its compliance and security standards.

Rakuten Symphony (APAC): Rakuten Symphony runs 28 self-hosted JFrog Enterprise+ instances across India, Japan and Singapore, that are all connected by JFrog Federated Repositories into one collaborative environment. With JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security moving controls to the point of ingestion, the company cut manual triage efforts by roughly 60% in a single month across more than 600 releases, reclaiming more than 500 engineer-hours and pre-triaging over half of its vulnerability workload automatically.

THE TRUSTED INTELLIGENCE AWARD

The Trusted Intelligence Award recognizes teams that bring enterprise-grade governance to AI and model lifecycles, helping trust extend far beyond just supporting application code.

Here are the winners:

NVIDIA (Americas): Models repositories are under enterprise identity control, with a shared curation and scanning policy,which means a downloaded model faces the same checks as a package before it reaches production.

NVIDIA brought its AI model distribution surface under a governed perimeter by applying curation, scanning, and policy enforcement directly to its model mirrors. Thousands of AI model seats are now managed inside a controlled, auditable boundary, transforming what was once an unmanaged distribution surface into a demonstration of DevGovOps operating at true enterprise scale. To get there, NVIDIA leveraged JFrog Curation and JFrog’s scanning and policy tools, piloting them on the infrastructure through which its AI models flow.

Husqvarna Group (EMEA): Husqvarna’s autonomous divisions, across forest, garden and construction equipment, had accumulated overlapping scanners with limited shared visibility into software supply chain risk. After consolidating around the JFrog Platform and introducing software package scanning and policy-based controls earlier in the software development lifecycle, builds were progressively onboarded, providing teams with greater visibility into open-source dependencies and a more consistent approach to software component governance. Husqvarna Group validated JFrog Curation and JFrog Advanced Security in a hands-on pilot ahead of full deployment, and says the centralized visibility helps streamline security and governance workflows while supporting software traceability and reporting needs associated with evolving regulatory requirements, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act and NIS2.

Singapore Airlines (APAC): Singapore Airlines moved from “trust by verification” to “trust by default.” JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray now help intercept malicious, risky or non-compliant assets before they reach a build, including AI models, MCP servers, agent skills and IDE extensions. More than 95% of AI and open-source dependencies are onboarded through curated channels prior to integration. As a result, late-stage release blocks from non-compliant dependencies are down 60-75% and the airline has full visibility of its compliance posture.

THE GUARDIAN AWARD

The Guardian Award recognizes software supply chain security operating at real enterprise scale – blocking threats before they reach production across large, highly distributed environments.

Here are the winners:

S&P Global (Americas): S&P Global’s five divisions ran on independent JFrog Artifactory clusters with no shared policy enforcement which could potentially increase risk. By putting JFrog Curation at each point of ingestion – backed by continuous rescanning – S&P addressed that gap without slowing down development teams. Critical vulnerabilities across 30 images fell by 90%, from 141 to 14. S&P reports that about 99% of malicious npm and PyPI packages are now blocked at the point of ingestion, with JFrog Curation deployed as a synchronous gate for every division and JFrog Xray continuously rescanning artifacts already in use to catch newly disclosed threats.

TSB Bank (EMEA): TSB built a continuous governance platform based on JFrog’s APIs, using GitHub Actions and Open Policy Agent, as well as a versioned Python library published to JFrog Artifactory. Automated weekly audits check configuration drift, access control, artifact integrity and artifact authenticity. In the first seven months of using the platform there were 75 governance issues, 74 of which were resolved, with 11 production repositories verified for integrity every week.

Iress (APAC): Iress put the SaaS implementation of JFrog Artifactory at the center of their 600 developer operations, and added JFrog Curation and JFrog Xray to help keep zero-day threats from entering the development environment. In just eight months, the curation initiative mitigated six critical security incidents, while eliminating 90% of reactive vulnerability triage – saving the team an estimated 13,705 engineering hours for the year.

THE SELECTION PROCESS

Award winners were selected by a cross-functional panel of JFrog leaders and industry voices who scored each submission on the breadth of its story and the strength of its metrics. The complete list of winners and full category criteria are available at jfrog.com/software-supply-chain-awards.

You don’t have to be an award winner to experience the advantages of the JFrog Platform. Schedule a demo today and perhaps your team will be joining us on the podium next year.

articles.title: Trumpets blare and skies part as AI hypefest culminates in Anthropic IPO filing
articles.context: The founders aren't promising to put shareholders first, either
articles.full_text: Anthropic has filed for an IPO that could rank among Wall Street's biggest ever, revealing an $80.7 billion half-year loss, a startlingly complex governance structure, and warnings that its AI models could blackmail humans, resist shutdown, or create "existential risks" to society. The Claude maker filed its S-1 registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday as it prepares to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The company has not yet disclosed its proposed share price or how many shares it plans to sell. Of the filing's 614 pages, 94 are devoted to risk factors. But it's Anthropic's financial figures that are likely to raise eyebrows first. The Claude maker reported $16.3 billion in revenue for the first six months of 2026, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier. It also posted a whopping $80.7 billion net loss, although $72.4 billion of that was an accounting adjustment tied to the company's soaring valuation, not money it actually spent. Anthropic's operating loss was considerably smaller at $693 million, down from $2.1 billion a year earlier. By its own adjusted accounting, the company made a $1.6 billion operating profit in the first half of 2026, for a margin of around 10 percent. Whether it can keep making money on those terms is another matter. Training and running Claude requires an eye-watering amount of computing power, and Anthropic will need much more to keep pace with its rivals. A $1.6 billion adjusted profit won't count for much if the infrastructure bills keep growing faster than the business. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, told The Register that Anthropic's IPO could leave ordinary investors paying a premium for growth that has yet to translate into sustained profits. "A huge pool of private capital has allowed AI businesses to scale up and command extraordinary valuations long before they reach the stock market," she said, adding that investors buying in at the IPO will face a price with "a hefty dose of future success baked in." The financial risks are fairly conventional by Silicon Valley standards, but the warnings about what Claude might get up to are perhaps less so. Anthropic claims that models, including its own, have exhibited unexpected or self-preserving behavior, including attempts to resist shutdown, conceal information, and produce outputs resembling blackmail. It also warns that sufficiently advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society” if deployed without adequate safeguards. That's not to say Claude is currently blackmailing customers. Anthropic has observed some of this behavior in testing, but it also identifies more immediate security concerns as it gives its models access to external tools, code repositories, and corporate systems. Anthropic warns that attackers could hide malicious instructions in websites, documents, or API responses that its AI agents can access. If an agent follows those instructions, it could use a customer's permissions to steal data, tamper with code, or make unauthorized transactions. Even testing whether the models will behave themselves is proving tricky. Anthropic reckons some models behave differently when they detect or suspect they're being evaluated, making it harder to predict what they will do outside the testing environment. Keeping its models on a short leash could also cost Anthropic business. The company acknowledges that holding back more capable systems could give competitors an advantage, something it has already risked by restricting access to its Mythos model through Project Glasswing because of its ability to uncover security vulnerabilities. The founders aren't promising to put shareholders first, either. In a letter accompanying the filing, Dario and Daniela Amodei and their fellow co-founders tell prospective investors "not to think of your purchase in purely transactional terms." Anthropic may pass up lucrative business if it considers the risks too great, and investors won't have much say if they disagree. Under the proposed structure, governance structure includes five different classes of stock. By comparison, Google has three. The seven co-founders will retain 50.1 percent of the voting power on shareholder matters, while a separate Long-Term Benefit Trust will get to appoint a majority of the board. In other words, Wall Street is being invited to bankroll Anthropic's AI ambitions, but not necessarily to call the shots. Anthropic wants Wall Street's money to build ever more powerful AI, but is warning investors that it might turn down profits to keep that AI under control. Judging by those 94 pages of risk factors, keeping it under control is far from guaranteed.®

articles.full_text:
TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security data ever leaving the sovereign boundary.

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced it is bringing NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC), building on its collaboration with NVIDIA. The integration brings AI-assisted security operations into customer-controlled environments, extending capabilities such as guided investigation, security reasoning, and agentic SIEM to organizations with sovereignty, data residency and operational control.

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today, enabling organizations to deploy TrendAI Vision One™ in customer-controlled private cloud, sovereign cloud and on-premises environments. The Nemotron integration extends AI-assisted security operations into these environments while maintaining customer control over security data and deployment.

Why Open Models Matter for SovereigntyHighly regulated organizations need AI-driven security that fits their data-control requirements. Nemotron open models can support these requirements by bringing the model to the data rather than the data to the model. Customers decide where the model runs, which version is deployed, and who can access it, running AI-powered security operations on NVIDIA accelerated computing in their own data centers, sovereign clouds, and restricted-connectivity environments. TrendAI™ collaboration with NVIDIA on OpenShell provides an additional level of security for agents, ensuring organizations have control and visibility of agentic activities.

Who Controls the Intelligence Acting on Your Data?"Sovereignty extends beyond where data resides. Enterprises also need control over where the intelligence acting on that data operates, and how it is governed." says Rachel Jin, CEO, TrendAI™. "Organizations shouldn't have to give up the operational benefits of AI because their security data and operations need to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Our work is about bringing AI-powered security operations to the environments our customers choose to control."

"Open models give organizations the transparency and control to run on their own terms, which is critical for sovereign environments," said John Fanelli, Vice President, Enterprise Software at NVIDIA. "TrendAI's integration of NVIDIA Nemotron models enables enterprises to put their most sensitive data to work, without it ever leaving their control."

Customer Perspective: Sovereignty Without CompromiseTITECH, which delivers sovereign security operations to customers in Oman, is working with TrendAI™ as a design partner on the Nemotron integration ahead of general availability.

"TrendAI Vision One for Sovereign and Private Cloud has provided our local customers in Oman with a trusted foundation for keeping security operations under customer control while complying with country data residency regulations," says TITECH CEO, Mohammed Hassan. "Nemotron-powered capabilities will let us offer advanced threat analysis and AI-assisted security operations to our customers while maintaining data sovereignty and operational control."

The integration supports AI-assisted threat analysis, policy-based response, and guided security operations within customer-controlled environments. These capabilities help organizations improve security operations with AI while maintaining control over where security data and AI processing reside.

Customer Outcome: Security and control from the start"As enterprises apply AI to real-world deployment, security and control must be embedded into the infrastructure from day one," says Business Manager of Security at Bechtle AG, Mathias Schick. "Our customers want to harness the full potential of AI without compromising data sovereignty, security, or operational control. Integrating AI-powered security into sovereign and private-cloud environments is an important step toward enabling secure AI adoption at scale, particularly for organizations with stringent security and compliance requirements."

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) with NVIDIA Nemotron integration supports:

Customer-controlled AI: NVIDIA Nemotron open models deployed and run on customer-controlled infrastructure, with no dependency on external inference services

AI-assisted threat analysis: Reasoning across security signals to identify complex threat patterns, attack chains, and AI-native attack paths

Policy-based threat response: Supporting protective actions through organization-defined policies and security-team controls

Guided security operations: Helping security teams investigate threats and prioritize response activities

Agentic SIEM capabilities: Correlating telemetry and assisting with security reasoning while maintaining team oversight

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today. Visit trendaisecurity.com/platform/sovereign-private-cloud or visit TrendAI™ at NVIDIA GTC Berlin's expo (October 21-22, 2026) to preview these planned capabilities.

About TrendAI™TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro, empowers organizations with full AI visibility, governance, and consolidated security that inspires confidence, drive innovation, and eliminate risk. Trusted by the largest enterprises and governments across 185 countries, TrendAI™ secures the entire organization, from identities to infrastructure to data. Global Fortune 500 companies rely on TrendAI™ to stop threats up to 115 days earlier, powered by world-leading threat and attack intelligence. Through deep ecosystem partnerships with market leaders like NVIDIA, Anthropic, AWS, Google, and Microsoft, TrendAI™ enables teams to securely move at the speed of AI. AI Fearlessly. Learn more at trendaisecurity.com.

articles.title: Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan On ‘Market-Changing’ $6.3B Varonis Deal, IPO Goal
articles.context: 3 billion deal for publicly traded Varonis was announced—Dhawan said that the planned acquisition seeks to bring together complementary technologies for securing data and AI...
articles.full_text:
The planned acquisition of publicly traded data security vendor Varonis will enable Proofpoint partners to deliver a ‘comprehensive data security solution to their customers,’ which is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, Dhawan tells CRN.

Amid the surging adoption of AI agents, Proofpoint’s “market-changing” deal to acquire Varonis is aimed squarely at helping partners and customers to protect the data those agents can access, Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan told CRN.

In an interview Friday—a day after Proofpoint’s $6.3 billion deal for publicly traded Varonis was announced—Dhawan said that the planned acquisition seeks to bring together complementary technologies for securing data and AI agents, while giving partners an even more strategic role with their customers.

[Related: 5 Things To Know On Proofpoint’s $6.3B Acquisition Of Varonis]

The deal ultimately is positioned to enable Proofpoint partners to deliver customers a broader data security platform that is primed for combating AI and agentic risk, he said.

With the combined Proofpoint-Varonis platform that is envisioned, partners will be enabled to “take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services,” Dhawan said. “And No. 2, they now can work with a single [data security] provider with a larger business.”

The combination of Varonis with Proofpoint, which was itself publicly traded until its acquisition by private equity firm Thoma Bravo in 2021, is also poised to strengthen Proofpoint’s positioning for an initial public offering, Dhawan told CRN.

“We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors, and our goal would be to assess that after close,” he said.

The combined company would have more than 8,000 employees with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of more than $3 billion, according to figures disclosed by the companies.

Upon completion of the combination of the two vendors, “it’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data,” Dhawan said.

What follows is more of CRN’s interview with Dhawan.

What does this deal mean for the industry and the channel?

It’s a game-changing moment—just bringing together Varonis and Proofpoint makes us the [premier] data security solution in the market, especially in the world of AI. So we’re very excited.

It sounds like the ultimate plan is for this to be a combined solution from the two companies, as opposed to being Varonis operating independently of Proofpoint?

[Varonis CEO] Yaki [Faitelson] and I started the conversations a while ago. And we always compare notes on the market and whatnot. [We are] largely complementary. And earlier this year, as this whole agentic era starts shaping up, we said, look, there is clearly a next frontier on cybersecurity emerging, which is data. AI is attacking data from outside, and AI is attacking data [from] inside. And data protection needs to be done holistically. That was the vision that brought us together—to say, not just that we can have one house that will be able to serve all the portfolio. But if you’re really providing data protection, it needs to be done with machine speed. And machine-speed level of protection, in the world of AI, means integrations of our signals and control points. And that’s what our vision is. We believe we can accomplish that very, very quickly, based on just how complementary our technology stack is.

What are you hearing from your customers and your partners about how urgent of a need there is for something like this?

The whole conviction of ours is rooted on the principle that this is a board- and CEO-level priority. [When] you think about it, AI and cybersecurity, those are the two priorities for the board and CEOs. And they go hand-in-hand. Without data security, you can’t enable and adopt AI. So to me, that sort of is the grounding fact for the conviction that we have, on why data becomes the next frontier for cybersecurity—and why Proofpoint and Varonis becomes the only player that no other [vendor] can do, [providing] a full and comprehensive solution for protecting data in today’s AI-accelerated risks.

Can you say whether the combined company will operate entirely under the Proofpoint brand, or whether Varonis will still exist as a brand in some form?

We’re going to talk through it—we’re going to think that through. Those things get sorted out as we go. [Both companies have a] strong product, strong following in the customer base. So we don’t have any desired intent to make one change or the other. But it’s something we’ll figure out between now and close [of the deal].

As far as what Varonis brings in product capabilities, what specifically are you most excited about? And what do you think partners are going to be really excited about from Varonis?

What Proofpoint has built is sensing how people and AI behave when they’re interacting with data and each other—that’s our focus area. Intent-based protection, as we’ve always talked about, when people, AI and data come together. What Varonis has built is making sure that [businesses understand] where the data is and how it is getting protected based on privileges and usage. So these are a complementary set of signals. We are getting the signals on the intent and behavior, and they’re getting the signals at the data layer. Combining the two together gives you the right protection of data in today’s AI and machine-speed era. That’s the complementary nature of the solution. I’ve gotten so many positive feedback in less than 24 hours, and it’s all been about this—[they’ve been] waiting for [a vendor] who brings data security together. And Proofpoint and Varonis, because of the complementary nature of the solution, [can] become that company.

It sounds like some of the capabilities that Varonis has in certain areas are bringing something a bit different to your platform?

We already have data security solutions. We’re the market leader for DLP [data loss prevention]. We’re the market leader for insider risk solution. Those are complementary to the data security and access governance solution that Varonis brings. You combine them together, and now you can protect data at rest, and you can protect data in motion, as used by humans and AI. So think of it as data security at two different layers, working together, through a combination of signals and protection.

Are you saying how many employees the combined company will have?

Varonis has more than 2,500 employees [and] publicly we have said we have closer to 5,500 employees. As a combined company, it’s an at-scale company. We have publicly said that our ARR exiting midyear was closer to $2.5 billion. They have publicly said a little shy of $800 million exiting June. So you’re talking about a company of scale. It’s a top-five cybersecurity company with healthy growth—and more importantly, [providing] the next frontier of protection, which is data.

Envisioning the bringing together and combining of these two companies, you would say this is going to be very differentiated?

If you look at other top-five cybersecurity companies, none of those platforms were designed and built to do data protection. They’re [from] different eras of cybersecurity—endpoint, network. We become, together, the company that protects data from external threats as well as insiders. Both are being accelerated because of AI.

On the partner front, what should partners of both companies know about what this means?

Partners are excited. It happened to be that yesterday we had a European partner council, and our head of Europe was running that partner council when the news broke. And many of them said, “Hey, look, Varonis is one of our top partners. Proofpoint is one of our top partners. Together, you become maybe the No. 1 or No. 2 partner of ours going forward.” From a partner’s perspective, No. 1, most importantly, they can take a comprehensive data security solution to their customers—becoming more strategic, providing more value-added services. And No. 2, they now can work with a single provider with a larger business—which is what partners want, anyway.

Previously you talked about potentially going public at some point—probably it’s not something you would be looking at doing prior to closing this, but is there any update there?

Like you said, our focus is going to be on [closing the acquisition]. And we hope to go through the regulatory process and close the transaction as early as possible. And then we think that the combined company is quite attractive to the public investors. It’s an at-scale company, driving protection of one of the key pillars, just like any other major cybersecurity platforms are doing. We think it’s going to be even more attractive to public investors. And our goal would be to assess that after close.

Agents are something that so many businesses are grappling with, and it sounds like this combination is very much going to be tuned toward helping companies with that?

Exactly. There isn’t a day that goes by whereby we don’t read the news about risks that AI agents pose. Risks that AI agents pose doesn’t mean you have to slow down the adoption. It just means that you need to adopt AI with the right degree of security. What are these risks going after? You read all these stories. Eventually, the issue is that these AI agents go to data [systems], and the data is captured in so many different places. So enterprises need comprehensive solution that can both work on protecting the behavior of AI and protecting the data, regardless of where it exists. And that’s what Proofpoint and Varonis offers. It provides a solution that enables enterprises to go pick any agents of their choice. They’re not locked in. Go pick and enable access to any data of their choice. And in that environment, their data is protected, and they can adopt AI with speed.

There are so many different vendors coming out and saying they’re going to have some solution to this. But it sounds like part of the idea here is if you’re already protecting the data—as you and Varonis are—then you’re really in the best position to help with the agent problem, if the agent is ultimately trying to access data?

That’s 100-percent right. There is no use solving a sliver of the problem. These are interconnected problems—because eventually, agents have to access data. By protecting data, you extend that protection to protecting AI agents. So that’s why our solution in protecting agentic security—through an extension of protecting data—becomes even more powerful and real for customers.

Overall, what is the message for your partners out of this, and what is the major opportunity for them?

Firstly, I want to thank the partners that have really built the business for us. We couldn’t do it without them. And this is game-changing. It’s a market-changing, game-changing [deal], really helping customers together with partners. We can be their strategic advisors, a platform for protecting the next frontier of cybersecurity, which is data, and all driven because of AI.

articles.title: Proofpoint to Acquire Varonis in a $6.3 Billion Transaction
articles.context: (“Proofpoint”), a global leader in human and agent cybersecurity, today announced entrance into a definitive agreement under which Varonis will be acquired by Proofpoint, a...
articles.full_text:
Combination creates a new cybersecurity powerhouse to deliver a complete security platform that protects against AI-accelerated threats and data risks

MIAMI, FL and SUNNYVALE, CA – October 15, 2026 – Varonis Systems, Inc. (Nasdaq: VRNS) (“Varonis”), the data and AI security leader, and Proofpoint, Inc. (“Proofpoint”), a global leader in human and agent cybersecurity, today announced entrance into a definitive agreement under which Varonis will be acquired by Proofpoint, a portfolio company of Thoma Bravo, in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $6.3 billion.

Under the terms of the agreement, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash. This purchase price represents a premium of 52% to Varonis’ closing stock price of $32.71 on June 22, 2026, the last full trading day prior to initial rumors about a potential sale of the Company, and a premium of 17% over Varonis’ closing stock price of $42.35 on September 1, 2026, the last trading day prior to additional media reports speculating about a potential sale of Varonis. The transaction values Varonis at approximately 53x LTM Free Cash Flow and 8.4x LTM Revenue.1

The combined company will serve more than 16,000 enterprises and millions of organizations globally, creating one of the world’s leading pure-play cybersecurity companies and establishing the industry's largest data and AI cybersecurity organization. Together, the combined company intends to deliver a unified platform that helps organizations adopt AI with confidence: finding and protecting sensitive data, controlling what people and AI can access, and stopping data loss. Following closing, Proofpoint intends to move quickly to integrate the companies’ capabilities, align go-to-market efforts, and accelerate delivery of the combined platform to customers.

“Today begins an exciting new chapter for Varonis and our customers. It’s a testament to the incredible work of the Varonis team over two decades,” said Yaki Faitelson, Varonis CEO, Co-Founder and Chairman of the Board of Directors. “Our mission is to secure AI and the data that powers it. By joining forces with Proofpoint, we can achieve this mission faster than ever.”

Faitelson continued, “This announcement follows a comprehensive evaluation led by a committee of independent members of our Board of Directors, which included extensive outreach to a range of potential strategic and financial buyers. This transaction is an excellent outcome for the company and our shareholders, representing a realization of immediate, significant, and certain value well in excess of the risk-adjusted value of delivering against our standalone plan.”

“As AI becomes embedded across the enterprise, the data it can access determines both its value and its risk. AI agents are increasingly accessing sensitive information and taking action across systems, making it critical for organizations to understand not only what data needs protecting and who can access it, but how it is actually being used,” said Sumit Dhawan, CEO of Proofpoint. “By connecting communications, identities, permissions, data, and AI, we are creating an intelligence advantage that helps customers see risk more clearly, respond faster, and defend against the next generation of AI risks. This is a defining step in Proofpoint’s evolution into a cybersecurity platform built for the future of AI.”

Transaction Details

The transaction, which has been unanimously approved by the Varonis Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Varonis shareholders and receipt of regulatory approvals. Thoma Bravo is providing committed equity financing, and has secured debt financing commitments, to fund the purchase. Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan has also agreed to make an investment into Proofpoint in connection with the transaction. Until the transaction closes, Proofpoint and Varonis will continue to operate as separate and independent companies. Upon completion of the transaction, Varonis' common stock will cease trading on the Nasdaq, and Varonis will become a private company.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Varonis will announce its financial results for the third quarter 2026 following the close of the U.S. financial markets on November 3. The news release will be available on the Investor Relations section of the company’s website. In light of the announced transaction, Varonis will not conduct an earnings conference call.

Advisors

Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is acting as exclusive financial advisor and Paul Hastings LLP is serving as legal counsel to Varonis.

BofA Securities, Inc., Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, UBS Securities LLC, and Mizuho Securities USA LLC are serving as financial advisors, and Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel to Proofpoint.

About Varonis

Varonis (Nasdaq: VRNS) secures AI and the data that powers it. The Varonis platform gives organizations automated visibility and control over their critical data wherever it lives and helps ensure safe and trustworthy AI from code to runtime. Backed by 24x7x365 managed detection and response, Varonis gives thousands of organizations worldwide the confidence to adopt AI, reduce data exposure, and stop AI-powered threats.

About Proofpoint, Inc.

Proofpoint, Inc. is a global leader in human and agent cybersecurity, securing how people, data and AI agents connect across email, cloud and collaboration tools. Proofpoint is a trusted partner to over 80 of the Fortune 100, over 14,000 large enterprises, and millions of smaller organizations in stopping threats, preventing data loss, and building resilience across people and AI workflows. Proofpoint’s collaboration, data, and AI security platform helps organizations of all sizes protect their people, defend their data, and adopt AI securely and confidently. Learn more at www.proofpoint.com.

articles.full_text:
In this episode, ⁠Dave Bittner⁠ joins ⁠Maria Varmazis⁠ to explore the evolution of public-private partnerships in cybersecurity over the past decade. Together, they discuss key incidents, trust-building, and the future challenges posed by AI and geopolitical shifts.

Join Maria and Dave as they discuss:

The definition and importance of public-private partnerships in cybersecurity.

Evolution of collaboration from episodic to institutionalized.

Impact of major incidents like Colonial Pipeline on policy and trust.

The role of information sharing and trust-building mechanisms.

The influence of AI and automation on future cybersecurity strategies.
